-O execfail: failed exec returns, USR1 trap restored

slicc-kernel#176 (shim-only proof on 1.26.6: shims/slicc/test/exec.test.mjs): exec readlink /proc/self == $$; 3-level exec bash chain keeps one pid; sh -c exec in a pipeline stage and a subshell exec keep that process's pid

/dev/tcp via the socket shim (netfork): realm-proxy round trip on 127.0.0.1:3128, $(hostname), refused port 'Connection refused', unknown host 'Name does not resolve', tailnet name dialled through the uplink (cert/net.mjs)

umask reaches the kernel (cert/umask.mjs, 5.3.0-10; slicc-kernel ≥ 1.35.1 kernelUmask): umask 077; : > f → 600 and /proc/self/status Umask 0077; umask 077; bash -c umask → 0077; umask 027 → touch 640, mkdir 750 (coreutils children); umask 077 → a WASIX child (perl open) creates 600; a subshell's umask does not leak back

pipes and close-on-exec (cert/pipes.mjs): (sleep 0.2; echo x) | cat ends; read + cat in a pipeline; a pipeline child holds 0 1 2 (+3, ls's own dirfd); exec 3>&1 → a child holds 0 1 2 3 (+4); seq 1 2000 through two cats

cert/jobs.mjs (5.3.0-11, Killed since -12): in an interactive pty, ^C typed right after Enter interrupts the new job 20/20 (rc 130); ^Z stops it 20/20 ('Stopped'), and `kill -KILL %1` on each stopped job (no SIGCONT) is reported 'Killed' 20/20. Patches: jobs-parent-terminal.patch (the shell gives the terminal to a new foreground job too: the kernel-forked child takes it tens of ms late) and jobs-notify-unqueue.patch (notify_of_job_status reaps a SIGCHLD that arrives while it prints). Prompts are matched as '[$#] ': since 5.3.0-13 the kernel's default user is root, whose prompt ends in '#'

cert/users.mjs (5.3.0-13, H1 homescoop#207, slicc-kernel >= 1.44.0): ids, names and prompts from the kernel's process credentials (shims/slicc/slicc_libc_gaps.c over Module.sliccKernel.cred()). As root: UID=0 EUID=0 GROUPS=0 HOME=/root USER=root, PS1 \u \$ -> 'root #', ~ = /root, ~cone = /home/cone, a file written in ~ reads back; as kernel.users.add({name:'cone'}): UID=EUID=1000 GROUPS=1000 100 HOME=/home/cone USER=cone, 'cone $'; interactive bash --norc -i in a pty prompts '[root]# ' and '[cone]$ '. File owners are the kernel's (1.44.0 stores none, uid 1000) and not checked

cert/sigint-line.mjs (5.3.0-15, readline-sigint-discard.patch): (1) 20 fresh pty shells, 'sleep 0.1 && echo ranN' + Enter and ^C 0..19 ms later: never a partial command (5.3.0-13: 'leep'); (2) 20 rounds of 'true' + Enter, ^C 1..5 ms later, then 'echo nextN': every next line runs (5.3.0-14 dropped it: it freed the line that arrived after a late ^C). The patch tags each readline line with a sequence number; the SIGINT handler records the line it belongs to (the one readline is returning if accept-line already ran, else the earlier one) and how many characters readline held; shell_getc frees only that line, and a later line runs whole minus those characters. On slicc-kernel main 749ab1e (#303) 3/3 runs pass; next-line phase alone, 40 rounds: -15 0 lost on main and on 1.47.1, -13 3 and 7
